stemMd: What is the domain of f(x) = 1/√(x − 4)?
explanationMd: A real square root requires x − 4 ≥ 0, but because it is in the denominator it must also be nonzero. Combining the conditions gives x − 4 > 0, hence x > 4.

distractorRationale.a: At x = 4 the denominator is zero.
distractorRationale.b: The radicand would be negative over the reals.
distractorRationale.c: Both the square root and denominator impose restrictions.
distractorRationale.e: This wrongly allows real x below 4.
